entities.name: Dénes Szécsi
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Dénes Szécsi de Felsőlendva (1410–1465) emerged as a pivotal figure in 15th-century Hungarian ecclesiastical and political life, serving as Archbishop of Esztergom from 1440 until his death. His tenure marked a critical period for the Hungarian Church, as he became the first Primate of Hungary in 1452, a title and set of rights personally bestowed by Pope Nicholas V. This elevation solidified the archiepiscopal see's authority and established a lasting precedent for the spiritual leadership of the realm, intertwining the ecclesiastical hierarchy deeply with the political fortunes of the Jagiellonian and Hunyadi dynasties.

Szécsi's political influence was substantial, particularly during the interregnum following the death of King Albert II. He championed the cause of the infant Ladislaus V Posthumus, playing a crucial role in his coronation as King of Hungary in 1440, despite the ongoing civil war. Later, as the most senior prelate, he performed the coronation of Matthias Corvinus in 1464, legitimizing the rule of one of Hungary's most celebrated monarchs. Beyond his political engagements, Szécsi was a dedicated churchman, instrumental in the restoration and embellishment of Esztergom Cathedral and a patron of the arts, contributing to the cultural flourishing of his archiepiscopal seat.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Dénes Szécsi's establishment of the Primacy of Hungary fundamentally reshaped the national church's structure and its relationship with both the papacy and the Hungarian crown. His direct involvement in royal coronations significantly influenced the political legitimacy of two monarchs, leaving a lasting impact on Hungarian statecraft.
